# Disclosed synthetic receive-verification corpus

`receive.json` is generated by `tests/receive_fixture.cpp` with the pinned native
Ryo SDK. All supplied addresses and private keys are deterministic test values
(e.g. view scalar 7, spend scalar 11, TX scalar 13); they are intentionally
public and must never hold funds. Signatures and range proofs are placeholders:
the generated transactions are serialization/derivation/amount containers,
**not consensus-valid chain transactions**. They are loaded only by tests.

The 31 cases cover clear v1/coinbase outputs, RingCT Full/Simple/Bulletproof
v2/v3 containers, standard/integrated/subaddresses, mixed recipients, zero and
above-JS-safe-integer amounts, additional/multiple main TX keys, three networks,
wrong/zero/noncanonical keys, missing/trailing bytes, hash/commitment/ECDH damage,
no match, Kurz/shared-key refusal and the unit-scalar subaddress edge case.

Two cases use the existing public genesis/v3 bytes from the native fixture
directory as parser/hash/no-match references only. No real receiving key or
ownership claim is invented for them. Native decodeRct/decodeRctSimple is an
independent known-amount oracle. The native CTest compares freshly generated
cases against this file; web tests replay exact native/WASM result parity.

Regenerate intentionally with the built `ryo_receive_fixture` executable:

```sh
ryo_receive_fixture web/tests/fixtures/receive.json tests/fixtures
```

Run both native and web tests after changing the corpus. Never replace test
scalars with wallet secrets, seeds or exports. See
[the approved verification boundary](../../../docs/LOCAL_RECEIVE_VERIFICATION.md).
